event.title: Pakistan Storm
event.summary: A suicide bombing targeted a mosque near a police facility in Kohat, Pakistan, resulting in at least 16 to 21 fatalities and numerous injuries. The attack involved a vehicle loaded with explosives, and gunmen reportedly attempted to storm the police compound during the incident. Among the casualties were police officers attending prayers at the mosque.

timeline.summary: Pakistan reported that airstrikes in Afghanistan resulted in the deaths of 28 militants in the border provinces of Kunar and Paktika. timeline.title: Suicide Bombing in Northwestern Pakistan Leaves 11 Dead
timeline.summary: A suicide bomb attack at a police checkpoint in northwestern Pakistan has resulted in at least 11 fatalities. The Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), also known as the Pakistani Taliban, has claimed responsibility for the attack, which reflects a rise in violence against security forces in the region.

event_overview.title: About Pakistan Storm
event_overview.subject: Pakistan Storm
event_overview.summary: “Pakistan Storm” is a tracking label for a September 2026 escalation centered on a deadly militant attack on a police complex in Kohat, northwestern Pakistan, and Pakistan’s subsequent military action across the Afghan border. It sits within a longer pattern of violence involving Pakistan-based militant groups and recurring Pakistan-Afghanistan cross-border hostilities, for which the sides have made competing claims about targets and civilian harm.

facts.label: Timeframe
facts.value: The selected developments run from September 18 through September 21, 2026; the incident sequence began with an attack at Kohat Police Lines and remained active as Pakistan announced strikes in Afghanistan.

facts.label: Location
facts.value: Kohat is in Pakistan’s northwestern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. The related military dimension concerns locations across the Pakistan-Afghanistan border, rather than a single battlefield or formally declared operation area.

facts.label: Kohat attack
facts.value: Pakistan’s government confirmed that a bomb blast struck the mosque at Kohat Police Lines during Friday prayers on September 18. Pakistani security forces subsequently conducted a clearance operation at the complex.

facts.label: Militancy context
facts.value: Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) has been listed by Pakistan’s Interior Ministry as a proscribed organization since August 25, 2008. Reporting on the Kohat attack linked the violence to militants operating in the border region, but responsibility and affiliations should be treated separately from official attribution and ongoing investigations.

facts.label: Cross-border context
facts.value: Pakistan-Afghanistan armed clashes and air operations predate this episode. UNAMA documented civilian casualties from cross-border fire and aerial attacks in late February and early March 2026 and called on all parties to meet their international humanitarian-law obligations to protect civilians.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the Kohat attack, its reported casualty updates, and the immediate Pakistan-Afghanistan escalation; it does not attempt to cover every militant incident in Pakistan, the full history of the TTP, or all prior cross-border clashes.
